1→name: Commit Lint
     2→
     3→on:
     4→  pull_request:
     5→    branches: [main]
     6→    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, edited]
     7→
     8→permissions:
     9→  contents: read
    10→  pull-requests: read
    11→
    12→jobs:
    13→  commit-lint:
    14→    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    15→    steps:
    16→      - name: Checkout code
    17→        uses: actions/checkout@v4
    18→        with:
    19→          fetch-depth: 0
    20→
    21→      - name: Validate PR title (conventional commit)
    22→        run: |
    23→          PR_TITLE="${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}"
    24→          echo "PR title: $PR_TITLE"
    25→
    26→          # Conventional commit pattern:
    27→          # type(scope)?: description  OR  type(scope)?!: description (breaking)
    28→          PATTERN='^(feat|fix|perf|refactor|test|docs|build|ci|chore|revert|style)(\([^)]+\))?!?\s*:\s*.+'
    29→
    30→          if echo "$PR_TITLE" | grep -qP "$PATTERN"; then
    31→            echo "PR title follows conventional commit format"
    32→          else
    33→            echo "::error::PR title does not follow conventional commit format"
    34→            echo ""
    35→            echo "Expected format: type(scope): description"
    36→            echo "  Types: feat, fix, perf, refactor, test, docs, build, ci, chore, revert, style"
    37→            echo "  Examples:"
    38→            echo "    feat: add BMAD slash commands"
    39→            echo "    fix(ci): resolve permission error in test workflow"
    40→            echo "    chore: update dependencies"
    41→            echo "    feat!: breaking change description"
    42→            echo ""
    43→            echo "Semver mapping:"
    44→            echo "  feat:  -> MINOR version bump"
    45→            echo "  fix:   -> PATCH version bump"
    46→            echo "  !:     -> MAJOR version bump"
    47→            echo "  other: -> no version bump"
    48→            exit 1
    49→          fi
    50→
    51→      - name: Validate commit messages
    52→        run: |
    53→          PATTERN='^(feat|fix|perf|refactor|test|docs|build|ci|chore|revert|style)(\([^)]+\))?!?\s*:\s*.+'
    54→          MERGE_PATTERN='^Merge '
    55→          REVERT_PATTERN='^Revert '
    56→
    57→          BASE_SHA="${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}"
    58→          COMMITS=$(git log "$BASE_SHA..HEAD" --format="%s")
    59→          ISSUES=0
    60→
    61→          while IFS= read -r msg; do
    62→            [ -z "$msg" ] && continue
    63→            if echo "$msg" | grep -qP "$PATTERN" || \
    64→               echo "$msg" | grep -qP "$MERGE_PATTERN" || \
    65→               echo "$msg" | grep -qP "$REVERT_PATTERN"; then
    66→              echo "  OK: $msg"
    67→            else
    68→              echo "  ::warning::Non-conventional commit: $msg"
    69→              ISSUES=$((ISSUES + 1))
    70→            fi
    71→          done <<< "$COMMITS"
    72→
    73→          if [ "$ISSUES" -gt 0 ]; then
    74→            echo ""
    75→            echo "$ISSUES commit(s) don't follow conventional commit format (warnings only)"
    76→            echo "PR title is the primary enforcement point for squash merges"
    77→          fi
    78→
    79→          echo ""
    80→          echo "Commit lint passed"

    28→      contents: read
    29→      pull-requests: write
    30→      checks: write
    31→    
    32→    steps:
    33→      - name: Checkout code
    34→        uses: actions/checkout@v4
    35→        with:
    36→          fetch-depth: 0
    37→
    38→      - name: Set up Python
    39→        uses: actions/setup-python@v4
    40→        with:
    41→          python-version: "3.13"
    42→
    43→      - name: Install dependencies
    44→        run: |
    45→          pip install uv
    46→          uv sync --frozen
    47→
    48→      - name: Run health check
    49→        id: health
    50→        run: |
    51→          echo "## 📊 Health Check Report" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
    52→          echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
    53→          
    54→          # Run health check and capture output
    55→          uv run python scripts/ci/daily_health_check.py --output json > health_report.json 2>/dev/null || true
    56→          
    57→          # Parse results
    58→          OVERALL_SCORE=$(cat health_report.json | python -c "import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin).get('overall_score', 0))" 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
    59→          UNTRACKED_COUNT=$(cat health_report.json | python -c "import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin).get('untracked_count', 0))" 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
    60→          SECURITY_HIGH=$(cat health_report.json | python -c "import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin).get('security_issues', {}).get('HIGH', 0))" 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
    61→          
    62→          echo "overall_score=$OVERALL_SCORE" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
    63→          echo "untracked_count=$UNTRACKED_COUNT" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
    64→          echo "security_high=$SECURITY_HIGH" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
    65→          
    66→          # Determine status
    67→          if [ "$SECURITY_HIGH" -gt 0 ]; then
    68→            echo "status=fail" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
    69→            echo "🔴 **Status: FAIL** - Security issues require attention" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
    70→          elif [ "$(echo "$OVERALL_SCORE < 0.5" | bc -l 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" -eq 1 ]; then
    71→            echo "status=warn" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
    72→            echo "🟡 **Status: WARNING** - Health score below 50%" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
    73→          else
    74→            echo "status=pass" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
    75→            echo "🟢 **Status: PASS** - Repository is healthy" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
    76→          fi
    77→          
    78→          echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
    79→          echo "| Metric | Value |" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
    80→          echo "|--------|-------|" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
    81→          echo "| Overall Score | $(printf '%.0f%%' $(echo "$OVERALL_SCORE * 100" | bc -l)) |" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
    82→          echo "| Security (HIGH) | $SECURITY_HIGH |" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
    83→          echo "| Untracked Files | $UNTRACKED_COUNT |" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
    84→
    85→      - name: Upload health report
    86→        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
    87→        with:
    88→          name: health-report
    89→          path: health_report.json
    90→          if-no-files-found: warn
    91→
    92→      - name: Comment on PR
    93→        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    94→        uses: actions/github-script@v7
    95→        with:
    96→          script: |
    97→            const fs = require('fs');
    98→            const health = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('health_report.json', 'utf8'));
    99→            
   100→            const statusEmoji = health.overall_score >= 0.8 ? '🟢' : 
   101→                                 health.overall_score >= 0.5 ? '🟡' : '🔴';
   102→            
   103→            const body = `## ${statusEmoji} Health Check Results
   104→            
   105→            | Category | Status | Score | Message |
   106→            |-----------|--------|-------|---------|
   107→            ${health.checks.map(c => 
   108→              `| ${c.category} | ${c.passed ? '✅' : '❌'} | ${(c.score * 100).toFixed(0)}% | ${c.message} |`
   109→            ).join('\n')}
   110→            
   111→            **Overall Score:** ${(health.overall_score * 100).toFixed(0)}%
   112→            
   113→            ${health.recommendations.length > 0 ? 
   114→              `### Recommendations\n${health.recommendations.map(r => `- ${r}`).join('\n')}` : 
   115→              '✅ No critical issues found.'}
   116→            
   117→            <details>
   118→            <summary>View Details</summary>
   119→            
   120→            \`\`\`json
   121→            ${JSON.stringify(health, null, 2)}
   122→            \`\`\`
   123→            </details>`;
   124→            
   125→            // Find existing comment
   126→            const { data: comments } = await github.rest.issues.listComments({
   127→              owner: context.repo.owner,
   128→              repo: context.repo.repo,
   129→              issue_number: context.issue.number,
   130→            });
   131→            
   132→            const botComment = comments.find(c => 
   133→              c.user.type === 'Bot' && 
   134→              c.body.includes('Health Check Results')
   135→            );
   136→            
   137→            if (botComment) {
   138→              await github.rest.issues.updateComment({
   139→                owner: context.repo.owner,
   140→                repo: context.repo.repo,
   141→                comment_id: botComment.id,
   142→                body: body
   143→              });
   144→            } else {
   145→              await github.rest.issues.createComment({
   146→                owner: context.repo.owner,
   147→                repo: context.repo.repo,
   148→                issue_number: context.issue.number,
   149→                body: body
   150→              });
   151→            }
   152→
   153→      - name: Check health threshold
   154→        if: steps.health.outputs.security_high > 0
   155→        run: |
   156→          echo "::error::Security issues found. Please address HIGH severity issues before merging."
   157→          # Don't fail the build - just warn
   158→          exit 0
   159→
   160→  # ── Security Scan ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   161→  security:
   162→    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
   163→    steps:
   164→      - name: Checkout code
   165→        uses: actions/checkout@v4
   166→
   167→      - name: Set up Python
   168→        uses: actions/setup-python@v4
   169→        with:
   170→          python-version: "3.13"
   171→
   172→      - name: Install bandit
   173→        run: pip install bandit
   174→
   175→      - name: Run security scan
   176→        run: |
   177→          bandit -r src/cohezion -f json -o security_report.json || true
   178→          bandit -r src/cohezion -f txt || true
   179→
   180→      - name: Upload security report
   181→        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
   182→        with:
   183→          name: security-report
   184→          path: security_report.json
   185→          if-no-files-found: ignore
   186→
   187→  # ── Daily Report ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   188→  daily-report:
   189→    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
   190→    if: github.event_name == 'schedule'
   191→    needs: [health, security]
   192→    
   193→    steps:
   194→      - name: Create issue for critical issues
   195→        if: steps.health.outputs.security_high > 0
   196→        uses: actions/github-script@v7
   197→        with:
   198→          script: |
   199→            await github.rest.issues.create({
   200→              owner: context.repo.owner,
   201→              repo: context.repo.repo,
   202→              title: '🚨 Critical Security Issues Detected',
   203→              body: `Automated health check detected critical issues.
   204→              
   205→              - Security HIGH issues: ${{ steps.health.outputs.security_high }}
   206→              - Untracked files: ${{ steps.health.outputs.untracked_count }}
   207→              - Health score: ${{ steps.health.outputs.overall_score }}
   208→              
   209→              Run \`uv run python scripts/ci/daily_health_check.py\` for details.`,
   210→              labels: ['security', 'needs-attention']

1→name: Repository Health Check
     2→
     3→# Session 55, Task #7: Repository health governance
     4→# Layer 2: Detection - automated repository size monitoring
     5→
     6→on:
     7→  push:
     8→    branches: [main]
     9→  pull_request:
    10→    branches: [main]
    11→  schedule:
    12→    - cron: '0 2 * * 0'  # Weekly Sunday 2am UTC
    13→  workflow_dispatch:  # Manual trigger
    14→
    15→jobs:
    16→  check-repo-health:
    17→    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    18→
    19→    steps:
    20→      - name: Checkout repository
    21→        uses: actions/checkout@v4
    22→        with:
    23→          fetch-depth: 0  # Full history for comprehensive analysis
    24→
    25→      - name: Check repository size
    26→        run: |
    27→          echo "=== Repository Size Analysis ==="
    28→          REPO_SIZE=$(du -sh .git | cut -f1)
    29→          echo "Repository size: $REPO_SIZE"
    30→
    31→          # Get size in bytes for threshold check
    32→          SIZE_BYTES=$(du -sb .git | cut -f1)
    33→          SIZE_GB=$((SIZE_BYTES / 1024 / 1024 / 1024))
    34→
    35→          echo "Size in GB: $SIZE_GB"
    36→
    37→          # Alert if >10GB (should be <6GB after Session 55 cleanup)
    38→          if [ "$SIZE_BYTES" -gt 10737418240 ]; then
    39→            echo "::error::Repository exceeds 10GB threshold ($SIZE_GB GB)"
    40→            echo "::error::Target size is <6GB. Review and cleanup required."
    41→            exit 1
    42→          fi
    43→
    44→          # Warning if >6GB
    45→          if [ "$SIZE_BYTES" -gt 6442450944 ]; then
    46→            echo "::warning::Repository size ($SIZE_GB GB) approaching 10GB limit"
    47→            echo "::warning::Consider running git gc or reviewing large files"
    48→          fi
    49→
    50→      - name: Check for large files in history
    51→        run: |
    52→          echo "=== Large Files in Git History ==="
    53→          echo "Finding all files >1MB in git history..."
    54→
    55→          git rev-list --objects --all | \
    56→          git cat-file --batch-check='%(objecttype) %(objectname) %(objectsize) %(rest)' | \
    57→          awk '$1 == "blob" && $3 > 1048576 {printf "%.2f MB: %s\n", $3/1048576, $4}' | \
    58→          sort -rn | head -20 > /tmp/large_files.txt
    59→
    60→          if [ -s /tmp/large_files.txt ]; then
    61→            echo "⚠️  Large files found in history:"
    62→            cat /tmp/large_files.txt
    63→
    64→            # Count files >1MB
    65→            LARGE_FILE_COUNT=$(wc -l < /tmp/large_files.txt)
    66→            echo ""
    67→            echo "Total files >1MB: $LARGE_FILE_COUNT"
    68→
    69→            # Warning if >50 large files
    70→            if [ "$LARGE_FILE_COUNT" -gt 50 ]; then
    71→              echo "::warning::High number of large files ($LARGE_FILE_COUNT)"
    72→              echo "::warning::Consider using git-lfs for binary files"
    73→            fi
    74→          else
    75→            echo "✅ No files >1MB found in git history"
    76→          fi
    77→
    78→      - name: Check pack efficiency
    79→        run: |
    80→          echo "=== Git Pack Efficiency ==="
    81→          git count-objects -vH
    82→
    83→      - name: Validate .gitignore coverage
    84→        run: |
    85→          echo "=== .gitignore Validation ==="
    86→          echo "Checking for common bloat patterns..."
    87→
    88→          PATTERNS=(
    89→            "*.pt"           # PyTorch checkpoints
    90→            "*.pth"          # PyTorch weights
    91→            "*.ckpt"         # TensorFlow checkpoints
    92→            "*.safetensors"  # Safetensors format
    93→            "*.bin"          # Binary model files
    94→            "logs/"          # Log directories
    95→            "checkpoints/"   # Checkpoint directories
    96→            "*.log"          # Log files
    97→            "tmp/"           # Temporary files
    98→            ".cache/"        # Cache directories
    99→          )
   100→
   101→          MISSING=()
   102→          for pattern in "${PATTERNS[@]}"; do
   103→            if ! grep -q "^${pattern}" .gitignore 2>/dev/null; then
   104→              MISSING+=("$pattern")
   105→            fi
   106→          done
   107→
   108→          if [ ${#MISSING[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
   109→            echo "⚠️  .gitignore missing recommended patterns:"
   110→            for pattern in "${MISSING[@]}"; do
   111→              echo "  - $pattern"
   112→            done
   113→            echo ""
   114→            echo "::warning::Consider adding these patterns to .gitignore"
   115→          else
   116→            echo "✅ .gitignore has all recommended patterns"
   117→          fi
   118→
   119→      - name: Check protected directories
   120→        run: |
   121→          echo "=== Protected Directory Check ==="
   122→          PROTECTED_DIRS=("_bmad" ".claude/commands" ".agent" "src/cohezion")
   123→          MISSING=()
   124→
   125→          for dir in "${PROTECTED_DIRS[@]}"; do
   126→            if [ ! -d "$dir" ]; then
   127→              MISSING+=("$dir")
   128→              echo "::error::Protected directory missing: $dir"
   129→            else
   130→              FILE_COUNT=$(find "$dir" -type f | wc -l)
   131→              echo "  $dir: $FILE_COUNT files"
   132→            fi
   133→          done
   134→
   135→          if [ ${#MISSING[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
   136→            echo ""
   137→            echo "::error::${#MISSING[@]} protected directory(ies) missing!"
   138→            echo "::error::Run recovery scripts or check recent commits for accidental deletion."
   139→            exit 1
   140→          else
   141→            echo "All protected directories present."
   142→          fi
   143→
   144→      - name: Upload health metrics
   145→        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
   146→        if: always()
   147→        with:
   148→          name: repo-health-metrics
   149→          path: /tmp/large_files.txt
   150→          retention-days: 30
   151→
   152→      - name: Repository health summary
   153→        if: always()
   154→        run: |
   155→          echo ""
   156→          echo "=== Repository Health Summary ==="
   157→          echo "✅ Size check: Completed"
   158→          echo "✅ Large files scan: Completed"
   159→          echo "✅ Pack efficiency: Measured"
   160→          echo "✅ .gitignore coverage: Validated"
   161→          echo ""
   162→          echo "For detailed governance, see: /tmp/repository_health_governance.md"

    12→#   - SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL: For failure notifications
    13→#   - SURREAL_URL: Live database endpoint
    14→#   - SURREAL_USER/SURREAL_PASS: Live credentials
    15→# =============================================================================
    16→
    17→name: SurrealDB CI/CD Pipeline
    18→
    19→on:
    20→  push:
    21→    branches: [main, develop]
    22→    paths:
    23→      - '**/surreal*/**'
    24→      - '**/persistence/**'
    25→      - '**/core/**'
    26→      - '.github/workflows/surrealdb*'
    27→      - 'pyproject.toml'
    28→      - 'Makefile'
    29→      - 'docker/surrealdb*'
    30→      - 'scripts/run-surreal-tests.sh'
    31→  pull_request:
    32→    branches: [main, develop]
    33→    paths:
    34→      - '**/surreal*/**'
    35→      - '**/persistence/**'
    36→      - '**/core/**'
    37→      - '.github/workflows/surrealdb*'
    38→      - 'pyproject.toml'
    39→  schedule:
    40→    # Nightly live tests at 2 AM UTC
    41→    - cron: '0 2 * * *'
    42→    # Weekly compatibility tests on Sundays at 4 AM UTC
    43→    - cron: '0 4 * * 0'
    44→  workflow_dispatch:
    45→    inputs:
    46→      test_stage:
    47→        description: 'Test stage to run'
    48→        required: true
    49→        default: 'all'
    50→        type: choice
    51→        options:
    52→          - all
    53→          - lint
    54→          - type-check
    55→          - unit
    56→          - integration
    57→          - benchmark
    58→          - live
    59→
    60→env:
    61→  COHEZION_CI: "true"
    62→  PYTHONUNBUFFERED: "1"
    63→  UV_SYSTEM_PYTHON: "1"
    64→  PYTEST_XDIST_AUTO_NUM_WORKERS: "auto"
    65→  PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST: "1"
    66→  # SurrealDB test configuration
    67→  SURREAL_NAMESPACE: test
    68→  SURREAL_DATABASE: test
    69→  SURREAL_USER: root
    70→  SURREAL_PASS: root
    71→
    72→# =============================================================================
    73→# STAGE 1: LINT AND FORMAT
    74→# =============================================================================
    75→jobs:
    76→  lint-and-format:
    77→    name: Lint & Format (Stage 1)
    78→    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    79→    timeout-minutes: 5
    80→
    81→    steps:
    82→      - name: Checkout repository
    83→        uses: actions/checkout@v4
    84→        with:
    85→          fetch-depth: 0
    86→
    87→      - name: Setup Python
    88→        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
    89→        with:
    90→          python-version: "3.13"
    91→
    92→      - name: Install uv
    93→        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
    94→        with:
    95→          version: "0.5.x"
    96→          enable-cache: true
    97→          cache-dependency-glob: "pyproject.toml"
    98→
    99→      - name: Sync dependencies
   100→        run: uv sync --frozen --group dev
   101→
   102→      - name: Run ruff format check
   103→        id: format
   104→        run: uv run ruff format --check --diff src/ tests/
   105→        continue-on-error: true
   106→
   107→      - name: Run ruff lint check
   108→        id: lint
   109→        run: uv run ruff check --output-format=github src/ tests/
   110→
   111→      - name: Check for unused imports
   112→        run: uv run ruff check --select=F401 --output-format=github src/ tests/
   113→        continue-on-error: true
   114→
   115→      - name: Generate lint summary
   116→        if: always()
   117→        run: |
   118→          echo "## Lint & Format Results" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   119→          echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   120→          if [ "${{ steps.format.outcome }}" == "failure" ]; then
   121→            echo "⚠️ **Format Check**: Failed (run 'make format' to fix)" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   122→          else
   123→            echo "✅ **Format Check**: Passed" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   124→          fi
   125→          if [ "${{ steps.lint.outcome }}" == "failure" ]; then
   126→            echo "❌ **Lint Check**: Failed" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   127→          else
   128→            echo "✅ **Lint Check**: Passed" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   129→          fi
   130→
   131→      - name: Upload lint results
   132→        if: always()
   133→        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
   134→        with:
   135→          name: lint-results
   136→          path: |
   137→            .ruff_cache/
   138→          retention-days: 7
   139→
   140→# =============================================================================
   141→# STAGE 2: TYPE CHECK
   142→# =============================================================================
   143→  type-check:
   144→    name: Type Check (Stage 2)
   145→    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
   146→    needs: lint-and-format
   147→    timeout-minutes: 10
   148→
   149→    steps:
   150→      - name: Checkout repository
   151→        uses: actions/checkout@v4
   152→
   153→      - name: Setup Python
   154→        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
   155→        with:
   156→          python-version: "3.13"
   157→
   158→      - name: Install uv
   159→        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
   160→        with:
   161→          version: "0.5.x"
   162→          enable-cache: true
   163→          cache-dependency-glob: "pyproject.toml"
   164→
   165→      - name: Sync dependencies
   166→        run: uv sync --frozen --group dev
   167→
   168→      - name: Run mypy strict
   169→        id: mypy
   170→        run: |
   171→          uv run mypy --strict \
   172→            --show-error-codes \
   173→            --pretty \
   174→            --show-column-numbers \
   175→            --show-absolute-path \
   176→            --error-summary \
   177→            src/cohezion/persistence/ \
   178→            src/cohezion/surreal* 2>&1 | tee mypy-report.txt || true
   179→
   180→      - name: Upload type check results
   181→        if: always()
   182→        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
   183→        with:
   184→          name: type-check-results
   185→          path: mypy-report.txt
   186→          retention-days: 7
   187→
   188→      - name: Check for errors
   189→        run: |
   190→          if grep -q "error:" mypy-report.txt; then
   191→            echo "Type errors found!"
   192→            cat mypy-report.txt
   193→            exit 1
   194→          fi
   195→          echo "No type errors found!"
   196→
   197→      - name: Generate type check summary
   198→        if: always()
   199→        run: |
   200→          echo "## Type Check Results" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   201→          if [ "${{ steps.mypy.outcome }}" == "failure" ]; then
   202→            echo "❌ **mypy**: Failed" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   203→          else
   204→            echo "✅ **mypy**: Passed" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   205→          fi
   206→
   207→# =============================================================================
   208→# STAGE 3: UNIT TESTS (Fast, no external services)
   209→# =============================================================================
   210→  unit-tests:
   211→    name: Unit Tests (Stage 3)
   212→    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
   213→    needs: type-check
   214→    timeout-minutes: 15
   215→    strategy:
   216→      fail-fast: false
   217→      matrix:
   218→        python-version: ["3.13"]
   219→        shard: [1, 2, 3, 4]
   220→
   221→    steps:
   222→      - name: Checkout repository
   223→        uses: actions/checkout@v4
   224→
   225→      - name: Setup Python ${{ matrix.python-version }}
   226→        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
   227→        with:
   228→          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
   229→
   230→      - name: Install uv
   231→        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
   232→        with:
   233→          version: "0.5.x"
   234→          enable-cache: true
   235→          cache-dependency-glob: "pyproject.toml"
   236→
   237→      - name: Sync dependencies
   238→        run: uv sync --frozen --group dev
   239→
   240→      - name: Run unit tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
   241→        run: |
   242→          uv run pytest -m fast \
   243→            --dist loadgroup \
   244→            --tx "4*popen//python=python${{ matrix.python-version }}" \
   245→            --rsyncdir src/ \
   246→            tests/unit/ tests/persistence/ \
   247→            -v --tb=short \
   248→            --junitxml=junit-unit-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml \
   249→            --cov=src/cohezion \
   250→            --cov-report=xml:coverage-unit-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml \
   251→            --cov-report=html:htmlcov-unit-${{ matrix.shard }}/ \
   252→            -x
   253→
   254→      - name: Upload test results
   255→        if: always()
   256→        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
   257→        with:
   258→          name: unit-test-results-${{ matrix.shard }}
   259→          path: |
   260→            junit-unit-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
   261→            coverage-unit-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
   262→            htmlcov-unit-${{ matrix.shard }}/
   263→          retention-days: 7
   264→
   265→      - name: Generate coverage summary
   266→        run: |
   267→          echo "## Unit Tests (Shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   268→          if [ -f coverage-unit-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml ]; then
   269→            coverage=$(grep -o 'line-rate="[0-9.]*"' coverage-unit-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml | head -1 | grep -o '[0-9.]*')
   270→            echo "📊 **Coverage**: ${coverage}%" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   271→          fi
   272→
   273→# =============================================================================
   274→# STAGE 4: INTEGRATION TESTS (With SurrealDB Container)
   275→# =============================================================================
   276→  integration-tests:
   277→    name: Integration Tests (Stage 4)
   278→    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
   279→    needs: [type-check, unit-tests]
   280→    timeout-minutes: 30
   281→    if: |
   282→      github.event_name == 'schedule' ||
   283→      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
   284→      needs.unit-tests.result == 'success'
   285→
   286→    services:
   287→      surrealdb:
   288→        image: surrealdb/surrealdb:v2.0
   289→        ports:
   290→          - 8000:8000
   291→        options: >-
   292→          --health-cmd "curl -f http://localhost:8000/health || exit 1"
   293→          --health-interval 5s
   294→          --health-timeout 3s
   295→          --health-retries 5
   296→          --health-start-period 10s
   297→        env:
   298→          SURREAL_USER: root
   299→          SURREAL_PASS: root
   300→        volumes:
   301→          - ${{ github.workspace }}/data/surreal-test:/my/surreal/data
   302→        # Security hardening
   303→        security-opt: no-new-privileges:true
   304→        # Resource limits
   305→        resources:
   306→          limits:
   307→            memory: 2g
   308→            cpus: "2.0"
   309→
   310→    steps:
   311→      - name: Checkout repository
   312→        uses: actions/checkout@v4
   313→
   314→      - name: Setup Python
   315→        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
   316→        with:
   317→          python-version: "3.13"
   318→
   319→      - name: Install uv
   320→        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
   321→        with:
   322→          version: "0.5.x"
   323→          enable-cache: true
   324→          cache-dependency-glob: "pyproject.toml"
   325→
   326→      - name: Sync dependencies
   327→        run: uv sync --frozen --group dev
   328→
   329→      - name: Wait for SurrealDB
   330→        timeout-minutes: 3
   331→        run: |
   332→          echo "Waiting for SurrealDB..."
   333→          for i in {1..30}; do
   334→            if curl -sf http://localhost:8000/health > /dev/null; then
   335→              echo "✓ SurrealDB is ready"
   336→              exit 0
   337→            fi
   338→            echo "Attempt $i/30..."
   339→            sleep 2
   340→          done
   341→          echo "✗ SurrealDB failed to start"
   342→          exit 1
   343→
   344→      - name: Initialize SurrealDB schema
   345→        run: |
   346→          if [ -f scripts/graphrag_schema.surql ]; then
   347→            echo "Loading schema..."
   348→            curl -X POST \
   349→              -u REDACTED \
   350→              -H "Accept: application/json" \
   351→              -H "NS: test" \
   352→              -H "DB: test" \
   353→              -d "$(cat scripts/graphrag_schema.surql)" \
   354→              http://localhost:8000/import || echo "Schema load skipped"
   355→          fi
   356→
   357→      - name: Run integration tests
   358→        env:
   359→          SURREAL_URL: ws://localhost:8000/rpc
   360→          TEST_WITH_LIVE_DB: "1"
   361→        run: |
   362→          uv run pytest -m integration \
   363→            --dist loadgroup \
   364→            -n auto \
   365→            tests/integration/ \
   366→            -v --tb=short \
   367→            --junitxml=junit-integration.xml \
   368→            --cov=src/cohezion \
   369→            --cov-report=xml:coverage-integration.xml \
   370→            --cov-report=html:htmlcov-integration/ \
   371→            --cov-append
   372→
   373→      - name: Upload integration results
   374→        if: always()
   375→        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
   376→        with:
   377→          name: integration-test-results
   378→          path: |
   379→            junit-integration.xml
   380→            coverage-integration.xml
   381→            htmlcov-integration/
   382→          retention-days: 14
   383→
   384→      - name: Generate integration summary
   385→        if: always()
   386→        run: |
   387→          echo "## Integration Tests" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   388→          echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   389→          echo "- **SurrealDB Version**: v2.0" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   390→          echo "- **Endpoint**: ws://localhost:8000/rpc" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   391→          if [ -f junit-integration.xml ]; then
   392→            tests=$(grep -o 'tests="[0-9]*"' junit-integration.xml | grep -o '[0-9]*')
   393→            failures=$(grep -o 'failures="[0-9]*"' junit-integration.xml | grep -o '[0-9]*' || echo "0")
   394→            errors=$(grep -o 'errors="[0-9]*"' junit-integration.xml | grep -o '[0-9]*' || echo "0")
   395→            echo "- **Tests Run**: $tests" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   396→            if [ "$failures" -gt 0 ] || [ "$errors" -gt 0 ]; then
   397→              echo "- **Status**: ❌ Failed ($failures failures, $errors errors)" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   398→            else
   399→              echo "- **Status**: ✅ Passed" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   400→            fi
   401→          fi
   402→
   403→# =============================================================================
   404→# STAGE 5: BENCHMARK TESTS
   405→# =============================================================================
   406→  benchmark-tests:
   407→    name: Benchmark Tests (Stage 5)
   408→    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
   409→    needs: [unit-tests, integration-tests]
   410→    timeout-minutes: 20
   411→    if: |
   412→      github.event_name == 'pull_request' ||
   413→      github.event_name == 'schedule' ||
   414→      contains(github.event.head_commit.message, '[benchmark]')
   415→
   416→    steps:
   417→      - name: Checkout repository
   418→        uses: actions/checkout@v4
   419→        with:
   420→          fetch-depth: 0
   421→
   422→      - name: Setup Python
   423→        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
   424→        with:
   425→          python-version: "3.13"
   426→
   427→      - name: Install uv
   428→        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
   429→        with:
   430→          version: "0.5.x"
   431→          enable-cache: true
   432→          cache-dependency-glob: "pyproject.toml"
   433→
   434→      - name: Sync dependencies
   435→        run: uv sync --frozen --group dev
   436→
   437→      - name: Run benchmark tests
   438→        run: |
   439→          uv run pytest -m benchmark \
   440→            --benchmark-only \
   441→            --benchmark-json=benchmark-results.json \
   442→            --benchmark-compare \
   443→            --benchmark-histogram=.benchmark-results/histogram \
   444→            tests/ \
   445→            -v --tb=short
   446→
   447→      - name: Upload benchmark results
   448→        if: always()
   449→        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
   450→        with:
   451→          name: benchmark-results
   452→          path: |
   453→            benchmark-results.json
   454→            .benchmark-results/
   455→          retention-days: 30
   456→
   457→      - name: Generate benchmark summary
   458→        if: always()
   459→        run: |
   460→          echo "## Benchmark Results" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   461→          if [ -f benchmark-results.json ]; then
   462→            echo "```json" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   463→            head -100 benchmark-results.json >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   464→            echo "```" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   465→          fi
   466→
   467→# =============================================================================
   468→# STAGE 6: LIVE TESTS (Nightly against real DB)
   469→# =============================================================================
   470→  live-tests:
   471→    name: Live Tests (Stage 6)
   472→    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
   473→    needs: [unit-tests, integration-tests]
   474→    timeout-minutes: 30
   475→    environment: live-testing
   476→    if: |
   477→      github.event.schedule == '0 2 * * *' ||
   478→      (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.event.inputs.test_stage == 'live') ||
   479→      (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.event.inputs.test_stage == 'all')
   480→
   481→    steps:
   482→      - name: Checkout repository
   483→        uses: actions/checkout@v4
   484→
   485→      - name: Setup Python
   486→        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
   487→        with:
   488→          python-version: "3.13"
   489→
   490→      - name: Install uv
   491→        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
   492→        with:
   493→          version: "0.5.x"
   494→          enable-cache: true
   495→          cache-dependency-glob: "pyproject.toml"
   496→
   497→      - name: Sync dependencies
   498→        run: uv sync --frozen --group dev
   499→
   500→      - name: Verify live DB connectivity
   501→        id: verify
   502→        env:
   503→          SURREAL_URL: ${{ secrets.SURREAL_URL }}
   504→          SURREAL_USER: ${{ secrets.SURREAL_USER }}
   505→          SURREAL_PASS: ${{ secrets.SURREAL_PASS }}
   506→        run: |
   507→          echo "Testing connectivity to live SurrealDB..."
   508→          # Convert ws:// to http:// for health check
   509→          HEALTH_URL="${SURREAL_URL/ws/http}"
   510→          if curl -sf "$HEALTH_URL/health" > /dev/null; then
   511→            echo "✅ Live DB is accessible"
   512→          else
   513→            echo "⚠️ Live DB health check failed (proceeding anyway)"
   514→          fi
   515→
   516→      - name: Run live tests
   517→        env:
   518→          SURREAL_URL: ${{ secrets.SURREAL_URL }}
   519→          SURREAL_USER: ${{ secrets.SURREAL_USER }}
   520→          SURREAL_PASS: ${{ secrets.SURREAL_PASS }}
   521→          TEST_WITH_LIVE_DB: "1"
   522→          PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST_LIVE: "1"
   523→        run: |
   524→          uv run pytest -m live \
   525→            --timeout=300 \
   526→            tests/ \
   527→            -v --tb=short \
   528→            --junitxml=junit-live.xml \
   529→            --cov=src/cohezion \
   530→            --cov-report=xml:coverage-live.xml \
   531→            --cov-report=html:htmlcov-live/
   532→        continue-on-error: true
   533→
   534→      - name: Upload live test results
   535→        if: always()
   536→        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
   537→        with:
   538→          name: live-test-results
   539→          path: |
   540→            junit-live.xml
   541→            coverage-live.xml
   542→            htmlcov-live/
   543→          retention-days: 30
   544→
   545→      - name: Notify Slack on failure
   546→        if: failure()
   547→        uses: slackapi/slack-github-action@v1
   548→        with:
   549→          payload: |
   550→            {
   551→              "text": "🚨 SurrealDB Live Tests Failed",
   552→              "blocks": [
   553→                {
   554→                  "type": "header",
   555→                  "text": {
   556→                    "type": "plain_text",
   557→                    "text": "SurrealDB Live Tests Failed",
   558→                    "emoji": true
   559→                  }
   560→                },
   561→                {
   562→                  "type": "section",
   563→                  "fields": [
   564→                    {
   565→                      "type": "mrkdwn",
   566→                      "text": "*Repository:*\n${{ github.repository }}"
   567→                    },
   568→                    {
   569→                      "type": "mrkdwn",
   570→                      "text": "*Branch:*\n${{ github.ref_name }}"
   571→                    },
   572→                    {
   573→                      "type": "mrkdwn",
   574→                      "text": "*Commit:*\n${{ github.sha }}"
   575→                    },
   576→                    {
   577→                      "type": "mrkdwn",
   578→                      "text": "*Workflow:*\n<${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}|View Run>"
   579→                    }
   580→                  ]
   581→                }
   582→              ]
   583→            }
   584→        env:
   585→          SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL: ${{ secrets.SURREALDB_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL }}
   586→
   587→# =============================================================================
   588→# COMPATIBILITY TESTS (Weekly against SurrealDB latest)
   589→# =============================================================================
   590→  compatibility-tests:
   591→    name: Compatibility Tests
   592→    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
   593→    needs: unit-tests
   594→    timeout-minutes: 30
   595→    if: |
   596→      github.event.schedule == '0 4 * * 0' ||
   597→      contains(github.event.head_commit.message, '[compat]')
   598→
   599→    services:
   600→      surrealdb-latest:
   601→        image: surrealdb/surrealdb:latest
   602→        ports:
   603→          - 8000:8000
   604→        options: >-
   605→          --health-cmd "curl -f http://localhost:8000/health || exit 1"
   606→          --health-interval 5s
   607→          --health-timeout 3s
   608→          --health-retries 10
   609→          --health-start-period 15s
   610→        env:
   611→          SURREAL_USER: root
   612→          SURREAL_PASS: root
   613→        security-opt: no-new-privileges:true
   614→
   615→    steps:
   616→      - name: Checkout repository
   617→        uses: actions/checkout@v4
   618→
   619→      - name: Setup Python
   620→        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
   621→        with:
   622→          python-version: "3.13"
   623→
   624→      - name: Install uv
   625→        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
   626→        with:
   627→          version: "0.5.x"
   628→          enable-cache: true
   629→
   630→      - name: Sync dependencies
   631→        run: uv sync --frozen --group dev
   632→
   633→      - name: Wait for SurrealDB (latest)
   634→        timeout-minutes: 5

Here are the bugs found in the diff:

---

**Issue 1 — `actions/checkout@v6` does not exist (large breaking change)**

Every workflow file in this PR bumps `actions/checkout` from v4 to v6. As of today (March 2026), `actions/checkout` is at v4. There is no v6. This will cause every single job in every affected workflow to fail at the checkout step with "Unable to resolve action".

Affected files (all of them): `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `claude-code-review.yml`, `claude.yml`, `codeql.yml`, `commit-lint.yml`, `dependency-review.yml`, `health-check.yml`, `lint.yml`, `portfolio-tests.yml`, `release.yml`, `repo-health.yml`, `security-scan.yml`, `semver-check.yml`, `surrealdb-tests.yml`, `test.yml`.

---

**Issue 2 — `actions/setup-python@v6` does not exist (large breaking change)**

Every workflow also bumps `actions/setup-python` to v6. The current latest is v5. There is no v6. Same failure mode as above — every job that tries to set up Python will fail.

Same broad set of workflow files.

---

**Issue 3 — `actions/setup-node@v6` does not exist**

`.github/workflows/portfolio-tests.yml` bumps `actions/setup-node` from v4 to v6. The current latest is v4. No v6 exists.

---

**Issue 4 — `actions/download-artifact@v8` does not exist**

`.github/workflows/surrealdb-tests.yml` bumps `actions/download-artifact` from v4 to v8. The current latest is v4. No v8 exists. This breaks the artifact aggregation/reporting job at the end of the SurrealDB test suite.

---

**Issue 5 — `slackapi/slack-github-action@v2` has a breaking API change**

`.github/workflows/surrealdb-tests.yml` bumps `slackapi/slack-github-action` from v1 to v2. The v2 release replaced the `payload` input with `payload-templated` and restructured how messages are sent. The existing step still uses the old `payload:` input:

```yaml
- uses: slackapi/slack-github-action@v2
  with:
    payload: |
      { ... }
```

In v2, `payload` is no longer the correct input name. The step will silently send nothing or fail, depending on whether the action errors on unknown inputs.

---

**Summary**

The most severe issues are Issues 1–4: non-existent action versions that will break CI entirely across virtually every workflow. Issue 5 is a real API-breaking change in a step that does exist at v2 but with a changed interface. This PR should not be merged as-is.

**PR:** #34 in manderson240/cohezion — Dependabot bumps 10 GitHub Actions versions
**CLAUDE.md files:** /home/mike-anderson/dev/cohezion/CLAUDE.md

**Issue:** `astral-sh/setup-uv` v5→v7 (skipping v6) in multiple workflow files. This is a 2-major-version jump. One reviewer noted it interacts with a `version: "0.5.x"` pin in surrealdb-tests.yml.

**Your task:**
1. Run `gh pr diff 34 -- .github/workflows/surrealdb-tests.yml .github/workflows/security-scan.yml` to see the changes
2. Read the relevant files to check how setup-uv is configured (does it pin a uv version?)
3. Dependabot only proposes versions that exist — so v7 is real. The question is whether the major version jump introduces breaking changes.
4. Check if CLAUDE.md says anything about uv version management
5. Score the issue:
   a. 0: False positive
   b. 25: Might be real
   c. 50: Real but nitpick
   d. 75: Highly confident
   e. 100: Absolutely certain

Return: the score (0-100) and your reasoning.

And more!** Sending data to Slack can now be done with the YAML format, and that data can be sent to [a Slack API method][methods] or [technique of choice](https://github.com/slackapi/slack-github-action/tree/main#sending-techniques) with the provided payload. And additional configurations can improve error handling or customize values between steps. Breaking changes happen with this update and recommended migration strategies are detailed below. Adding this step to new workflows might prefer to follow the [`README`](https://github.com/slackapi/slack-github-action/tree/main#slack-send-github-action) instead :books: ## What's changed Both inputs of payload variables, techniques for sending the payload, additional configurations, and expected outputs were changed: - **Sending variables** - Breaking changes - [Only one payload input can be provided](#only-one-payload-input-can-be-provided) - [Only one technique to send can be provided](#only-one-technique-to-send-can-be-provided) - [Variable replacements no longer happen by default](#variable-replacements-no-longer-happen-by-default) - [Payload file path parsed option was removed](#payload-file-path-parsed-option-was-removed) - Enhancements - [Payloads can now be written in YAML](#payloads-can-now-be-written-in-yaml) - [Payload can now be written in unwrapped JSON](#payload-can-now-be-written-in-unwrapped-json) - **Sending techniques** - Technique 1: Slack Workflow Builder - Breaking changes - [The webhook type must be specified in webhook inputs](#the-webhook-type-must-be-specified-in-webhook-inputs) - [Payload flattening no longer happens by default](#payload-flattening-no-longer-happens-by-default) - Enhancements - [The webhook URL can be specified in webhook inputs](#the-webhook-url-can-be-specified-in-webhook-inputs) - Technique 2: Slack API method - Breaking changes - [The Slack API method now must be specified in inputs](#the-slack-api-method-now-must-be-specified-in-inputs) - [A token must be provided with other inputs](#a-token-must-be-provided-with-other-inputs) - [Inputs to the Slack API method must be provided in payloads](#inputs-to-the-slack-api-method-must-be-provided-in-payloads) - [Messages cannot be sent to multiple channels in one step](#messages-cannot-be-sent-to-multiple-channels-in-one-step) - Technique 3: Slack incoming webhook - Breaking changes - [The webhook type must be specified for incoming webhooks](#the-webhook-type-must-be-specified-for-incoming-webhooks) - Enhancements - [The webhook URL can be specified for incoming webhook](#the-webhook-url-can-be-specified-for-incoming-webhooks) - **Additional configurations** - Enhancements - [Steps can exit with an error after a failed Slack API call](#steps-can-exit-with-an-error-after-a-failed-slack-api-call) - [Failed requests can be retried various amounts of times](#failed-requests-can-be-retried-various-amounts-of-times) - [Provided payloads can be flattened with a delimiter](#provided-payloads-can-be-flattened-with-a-delimiter) - [Provided payloads can have templated variables replaced](#provided-payloads-can-have-templated-variables-replaced) - [Proxying HTTPS requests can be done within inputs](#proxying-https-requests-can-be-done-within-inputs) - **Expected outputs** - Breaking changes - [The time value is now returned as the Unix epoch time](#the-time-value-is-now-returned-as-the-unix-epoch-time) - Enhancements - [An ok value is added to represent response success](#an-ok-value-is-added-to-represent-response-success) - [A response value is added with the response data](#a-response-value-is-added-with-the-response-data) The following sections detail these changes with recommended changes for existing GitHub workflows using this step and certain features. If something seems off after making these changes, please feel free to [open an issue][issues] for discussion! 👾 ## Sending variables The source of variables remains the same, using one of the following inputs: - `payload`: Inputs written inline in your GitHub workflow file. - `payload-file-path`: Inputs gathered from a file. - **No input**: Uses the default event [context][event-context] with a [payload][event-payload] matching the GitHub event. ### :warning: Breaking changes
#### Only one payload input can be provided This Action now exits with an error if both `payload` and `payload-file-path` are provided. **Prior to updating**: Both options could be provided with `payload` being preferred. **Recommended change**: Use either `payload`, `payload-file-path`, or neither, when providing inputs. But don't include both.
#### Only one technique to send can be provided This Action now exits with an error if both `method` and `webhook` techniques are provided. **Prior to updating**: Both techniques could be used to send the same payload. **Recommended change**: Use either `method` or `webhook` to send data, but not both.
#### Variable replacements no longer happen by default This Action now sends payload provided in a `payload-file-path` file exactly as is. **Prior to updating**: Templatized variables in input files were replaced with the matching `github` or `env` variable: ```json { "channel": "${{ env.SLACK_CHANNEL_ID }}", "text": "A commit was made: ${{ github.sha }}" } ```

# /learn - Online Learning System

**Extract reusable knowledge from this session into skills.** Evaluates what was learned, checks for existing skills, and creates new ones when valuable patterns are discovered.

---

## TABLE OF CONTENTS

| Phase       | Description                                            | Steps   |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ------- |
| **Phase 0** | Reference: triggers, quality criteria, skill structure | 0.1–0.4 |
| **Phase 1** | Evaluate: assess if knowledge is worth extracting      | 1.1     |
| **Phase 2** | Check Existing: search for related skills              | 2.1     |
| **Phase 3** | Create Skill: write the skill file                     | 3.1–3.2 |
| **Phase 4** | Quality Gates: final checklist before saving           | 4.1     |

**Quick Step Reference:**

- 0.1 Triggers, 0.2 Quality criteria, 0.3 What NOT to extract, 0.4 Skill structure
- 1.1 Self-evaluation questions
- 2.1 Search existing skills
- 3.1 Choose location, 3.2 Write SKILL.md
- 4.1 Final checklist

---

## PHASE 0: REFERENCE

### Step 0.1: Triggers

Invoke `/learn` after ANY task involving:

| Trigger                      | Example                                                          |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Non-obvious debugging**    | Spent 10+ minutes investigating; solution wasn't in docs         |
| **Misleading errors**        | Error message pointed wrong direction; found real cause          |
| **Workarounds**              | Found limitation and creative solution                           |
| **Tool integration**         | Figured out how to use tool/API in undocumented way              |
| **Trial-and-error**          | Tried multiple approaches before finding what worked             |
| **Repeatable workflow**      | Multi-step task that will recur; worth standardizing             |
| **External service queries** | Fetched data from Jira, GitHub, Confluence, or other APIs        |
| **User-facing automation**   | Built something user will ask for again (reports, status checks) |

### Step 0.2: Quality Criteria

Skills must be:

- **Reusable**: Will help with future tasks (not just this instance)
- **Non-trivial**: Required discovery, OR is a valuable workflow pattern
- **Verified**: Solution actually worked, not theoretical

### Step 0.3: What NOT to Extract

- Single-step tasks with no workflow value
- One-off fixes unlikely to recur
- Knowledge easily found in official docs

### Step 0.4: Skill Structure

**Location:** `.claude/skills/[skill-name]/SKILL.md`

**Template:**

```markdown
---
name: descriptive-kebab-case-name
description: |
  [CRITICAL: This determines when the skill triggers. Include:]
  - What the skill does
  - Specific trigger conditions (exact error messages, symptoms)
  - When to use it (contexts, scenarios)
author: Claude Code
version: 1.0.0
---

# Skill Name

## Problem

[Clear description of the problem]

## Context / Trigger Conditions

[When to use - exact error messages, symptoms, scenarios]

## Solution

[Step-by-step solution]

## Verification

[How to verify it worked]

## Example

[Concrete example]

## References

[Links to documentation]
```

<details>
<summary>Writing Effective Descriptions</summary>

The description field is CRITICAL for skill discovery:

**Good:**

```yaml
description: |
  Fix for "ENOENT: no such file or directory" errors in npm monorepos.
  Use when: (1) npm run fails with ENOENT, (2) paths work in root but
  not in packages, (3) symlinked dependencies cause failures.
```

**Bad:**

```yaml
description: Helps with npm problems in monorepos.
```

</details>

**Guidelines:**

- **Concise** - Claude is smart; only add what it doesn't know
- **Under 500 lines** - Move large docs to `references/`
- **Examples over explanations** - Show, don't tell

---

## PHASE 1: EVALUATE

### Step 1.1: Self-Evaluation Questions

Ask yourself:

1. "What did I just learn that wasn't obvious before starting?"
2. "Would future-me benefit from having this documented?"
3. "Was the solution non-obvious from documentation alone?"
4. "Is this a multi-step workflow I'd repeat on similar tasks?"
5. "Did I query an external service the user will ask about again?"

**If NO to all → Skip extraction, nothing to learn.**

**Note:** External service queries (Jira tickets, GitHub PRs, Confluence pages) are almost always worth extracting - users frequently repeat these requests.

---

### Step 2.1: Search for Related Skills

Before creating, search for related skills:

```bash
ls .claude/skills/ 2>/dev/null
rg -i "keyword" .claude/skills/ 2>/dev/null
ls ~/.claude/pilot/skills/ 2>/dev/null
rg -i "keyword" ~/.claude/pilot/skills/ 2>/dev/null
```

| Found                | Action                           |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| Nothing related      | Create new skill                 |
| Same trigger and fix | Update existing (bump version)   |
| Partial overlap      | Update existing with new variant |

---

## PHASE 3: CREATE SKILL

### Step 3.1: Choose Location

**Project skills**: `.claude/skills/[skill-name]/SKILL.md`

### Step 3.2: Write SKILL.md

Use the template from Step 0.4. Ensure the description field contains specific trigger conditions.

---

## PHASE 4: QUALITY GATES

### Step 4.1: Final Checklist

Before finalizing:

- [ ] Description contains specific trigger conditions
- [ ] Solution verified to work
- [ ] Content specific enough to be actionable
- [ ] Content general enough to be reusable
- [ ] No sensitive information

---

**Skill Created**: `.claude/skills/lsp-dead-code-finder/SKILL.md`

```markdown
description: |

  function with only 1 reference (definition) or only test refs is dead code.
---

# LSP Dead Code Finder

...
```

---

## REMEMBER

**Continuous improvement.** Every valuable discovery should benefit future sessions.
Evaluate after significant work. Extract selectively. Create carefully.

# Dependabot AI Review Bias

## Problem

When multi-agent AI code review pipelines review Dependabot PRs, agents with stale
training data (knowledge cutoffs) will **confidently but incorrectly** flag proposed
version bumps as "non-existent." This creates false blocking findings that look credible
because the agents cite specific evidence ("current latest is v4, v6 does not exist").

## Context / Trigger Conditions

- Reviewing a Dependabot PR that bumps GitHub Actions to major versions
- AI review agents flag something like "actions/checkout@v6 does not exist" or
  "this version has not been released"
- Multiple agents disagree on whether a version exists
- Dependabot PR is from a date well past the reviewing agents' knowledge cutoffs

## Root Cause

Dependabot uses live GitHub API calls to discover available versions — it will NEVER
propose a version that doesn't exist as a real tag/release. AI review agents, by
contrast, have static training data with knowledge cutoffs. An agent trained in 2025
has no knowledge of 2026 GitHub Actions releases, but will confidently state they
don't exist rather than expressing uncertainty.

**The asymmetry:**
| Source | Data freshness | Reliability for version existence |
|--------|---------------|----------------------------------|
| Dependabot | Live GitHub API | **Authoritative** — version must exist |
| AI review agent | Training cutoff (static) | Unreliable — may predate the release |

## Solution

When an AI agent flags a Dependabot-proposed version as non-existent:

1. **Treat it as a false positive** — Dependabot cannot propose non-existent versions
2. **Discard the finding** — it does not need to be investigated further
3. **Focus on behavioral changes** — the real risk in major version bumps is breaking
   API changes, not the existence of the version

### What to Actually Review in Dependabot Action Bumps

Instead of checking if versions exist, check:
- **Breaking input changes**: Do any `with:` parameters change between versions?
- **Removed/renamed inputs**: Does the action's API surface change?
- **Node runtime requirements**: Some v7+ actions require Node 24 (default since March 2026)
- **Deprecated parameter warnings**: Will existing `with:` params silently do nothing?

## Known Breaking Changes (GitHub Actions)

### slackapi/slack-github-action v1 → v2

**Breaking change**: v1 accepted `payload:` as a standalone input with a raw JSON block.
v2 requires a *technique* to be specified — either:
- `webhook:` + `payload:` (for incoming webhooks), OR
- `method: chat.postMessage` + `token:` (for bot token API)

**Symptom**: Slack notifications stop working when tests fail. The step errors out
because no technique is configured.

**Pattern that breaks:**
```yaml
# BROKEN in v2 — missing webhook: or method: + token:
- uses: slackapi/slack-github-action@v2
  with:
    payload: |
      { "text": "Build failed" }
```

**Fix:**
```yaml
# CORRECT — specify webhook technique
- uses: slackapi/slack-github-action@v2
  with:
    webhook: ${{ secrets.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL }}
    webhook-type: incoming-webhook
    payload: |
      { "text": "Build failed" }
```

Note: This issue only triggers on the `if: failure()` path, so it won't break normal
CI — it only breaks Slack failure notifications.

## Verification

To verify a proposed version actually exists:
```bash
# Check GitHub releases for an action
gh api repos/actions/checkout/releases --jq '.[].tag_name' | head -5
gh api repos/slackapi/slack-github-action/releases --jq '.[].tag_name' | head -5
```

Dependabot's proposal is itself the verification — but if in doubt, use `gh api`.

## Example

During review of a 2026 Dependabot PR (PR #34 in cohezion):
- Agent #2 flagged: "actions/checkout@v6 does not exist — current latest is v4"
- Agent #4 flagged: "actions/setup-node@v6 does not exist"
- Agent #3 verified live: both v6 tags exist (v6.0.2 and v6.3.0 respectively)

All "version does not exist" findings were false positives. The only real issue was
`slackapi/slack-github-action` v1→v2 (a genuine breaking API change scored 75/100
— real but only triggers on failure path).

## References

- Dependabot version resolution: https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/dependabot-version-updates/about-dependabot-version-updates
- slackapi/slack-github-action v2 migration: https://github.com/slackapi/slack-github-action/releases/tag/v2.0.0

The key insight extracted: **Dependabot is authoritative about version existence; AI review agents with knowledge cutoffs are not.** When these two sources conflict, Dependabot wins — always. The "version does not exist" finding class should be treated as a false positive category in Dependabot PR reviews, and reviewers should focus energy on actual behavioral changes (breaking inputs, renamed parameters, runtime requirements) instead.

content.text:
Provide a code review for the given pull request.

To do this, follow these steps precisely:

1. Use a Haiku agent to check if the pull request (a) is closed, (b) is a draft, (c) does not need a code review (eg. because it is an automated pull request, or is very simple and obviously ok), or (d) already has a code review from you from earlier. If so, do not proceed.
2. Use another Haiku agent to give you a list of file paths to (but not the contents of) any relevant CLAUDE.md files from the codebase: the root CLAUDE.md file (if one exists), as well as any CLAUDE.md files in the directories whose files the pull request modified
3. Use a Haiku agent to view the pull request, and ask the agent to return a summary of the change
4. Then, launch 5 parallel Sonnet agents to independently code review the change. The agents should do the following, then return a list of issues and the reason each issue was flagged (eg. CLAUDE.md adherence, bug, historical git context, etc.):
   a. Agent #1: Audit the changes to make sure they compily with the CLAUDE.md. Note that CLAUDE.md is guidance for Claude as it writes code, so not all instructions will be applicable during code review.
   b. Agent #2: Read the file changes in the pull request, then do a shallow scan for obvious bugs. Avoid reading extra context beyond the changes, focusing just on the changes themselves. Focus on large bugs, and avoid small issues and nitpicks. Ignore likely false positives.
   c. Agent #3: Read the git blame and history of the code modified, to identify any bugs in light of that historical context
   d. Agent #4: Read previous pull requests that touched these files, and check for any comments on those pull requests that may also apply to the current pull request.
   e. Agent #5: Read code comments in the modified files, and make sure the changes in the pull request comply with any guidance in the comments.
5. For each issue found in #4, launch a parallel Haiku agent that takes the PR, issue description, and list of CLAUDE.md files (from step 2), and returns a score to indicate the agent's level of confidence for whether the issue is real or false positive. To do that, the agent should score each issue on a scale from 0-100, indicating its level of confidence. For issues that were flagged due to CLAUDE.md instructions, the agent should double check that the CLAUDE.md actually calls out that issue specifically. The scale is (give this rubric to the agent verbatim):
   a. 0: Not confident at all. This is a false positive that doesn't stand up to light scrutiny, or is a pre-existing issue.
   b. 25: Somewhat confident. This might be a real issue, but may also be a false positive. The agent wasn't able to verify that it's a real issue. If the issue is stylistic, it is one that was not explicitly called out in the relevant CLAUDE.md.
   c. 50: Moderately confident. The agent was able to verify this is a real issue, but it might be a nitpick or not happen very often in practice. Relative to the rest of the PR, it's not very important.
   d. 75: Highly confident. The agent double checked the issue, and verified that it is very likely it is a real issue that will be hit in practice. The existing approach in the PR is insufficient. The issue is very important and will directly impact the code's functionality, or it is an issue that is directly mentioned in the relevant CLAUDE.md.
   e. 100: Absolutely certain. The agent double checked the issue, and confirmed that it is definitely a real issue, that will happen frequently in practice. The evidence directly confirms this.
6. Filter out any issues with a score less than 80. If there are no issues that meet this criteria, do not proceed.
7. Use a Haiku agent to repeat the eligibility check from #1, to make sure that the pull request is still eligible for code review.
8. Finally, use the gh bash command to comment back on the pull request with the result. When writing your comment, keep in mind to:
   a. Keep your output brief
   b. Avoid emojis
   c. Link and cite relevant code, files, and URLs

Examples of false positives, for steps 4 and 5:

- Pre-existing issues
- Something that looks like a bug but is not actually a bug
- Pedantic nitpicks that a senior engineer wouldn't call out
- Issues that a linter, typechecker, or compiler would catch (eg. missing or incorrect imports, type errors, broken tests, formatting issues, pedantic style issues like newlines). No need to run these build steps yourself -- it is safe to assume that they will be run separately as part of CI.
- General code quality issues (eg. lack of test coverage, general security issues, poor documentation), unless explicitly required in CLAUDE.md
- Issues that are called out in CLAUDE.md, but explicitly silenced in the code (eg. due to a lint ignore comment)
- Changes in functionality that are likely intentional or are directly related to the broader change
- Real issues, but on lines that the user did not modify in their pull request

Notes:

- Do not check build signal or attempt to build or typecheck the app. These will run separately, and are not relevant to your code review.
- Use `gh` to interact with Github (eg. to fetch a pull request, or to create inline comments), rather than web fetch
- Make a todo list first
- You must cite and link each bug (eg. if referring to a CLAUDE.md, you must link it)
- For your final comment, follow the following format precisely (assuming for this example that you found 3 issues):

---

### Code review

Found 3 issues:

1. <brief description of bug> (CLAUDE.md says "<...>")

<link to file and line with full sha1 + line range for context, note that you MUST provide the full sha and not use bash here, eg. https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/1d54823877c4de72b2316a64032a54afc404e619/README.md#L13-L17>

2. <brief description of bug> (some/other/CLAUDE.md says "<...>")

<link to file and line with full sha1 + line range for context>

3. <brief description of bug> (bug due to <file and code snippet>)

<link to file and line with full sha1 + line range for context>

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)

<sub>- If this code review was useful, please react with 👍. Otherwise, react with 👎.</sub>

---

- Or, if you found no issues:

---

### Code review

No issues found. Checked for bugs and CLAUDE.md compliance.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)

- When linking to code, follow the following format precisely, otherwise the Markdown preview won't render correctly: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-cli-internal/blob/c21d3c10bc8e898b7ac1a2d745bdc9bc4e423afe/package.json#L10-L15
  - Requires full git sha
  - You must provide the full sha. Commands like `https://github.com/owner/repo/blob/$(git rev-parse HEAD)/foo/bar` will not work, since your comment will be directly rendered in Markdown.
  - Repo name must match the repo you're code reviewing
  - # sign after the file name
  - Line range format is L[start]-L[end]
  - Provide at least 1 line of context before and after, centered on the line you are commenting about (eg. if you are commenting about lines 5-6, you should link to `L4-7`)

- **185 total FLUME tests** (158 existing + 27 new)

     3→Maps compound execution quality metrics to 12D FLUME axiomatic trajectories
     4→using semantic embeddings and operation-specific modulation profiles.
     5→
     6→Lifecycle:
     7→  1. Extract execution metrics (coherence, efficiency, duration)
     8→  2. Generate semantic embedding from task description
     9→  3. Project to 12D using holographic method (2048D → 12D)
    10→  4. Apply operation-specific modulation (generate/analyze/search/etc)
    11→  5. Compute trajectory quality score (coherence*0.5 + smoothness*0.3 + convergence*0.2)
    12→  6. Persist journey point for experience-guided execution
    13→
    14→Features:
    15→- Deterministic 12D trajectory representation
    16→- Operation-aware modulation profiles
    17→- Holographic projection fallback (pure Python, no dependencies)
    18→- Comprehensive trajectory quality metrics
    19→- Experience guidance for future runs
    20→"""
    21→
    22→import hashlib
    23→import logging
    24→from dataclasses import dataclass
    25→from enum import Enum
    26→from typing import Any
    27→
    28→import numpy as np

    41→    SEARCH = "search"  # High spatial

   236→    def _text_to_latent(self, text: str) -> np.ndarray:
   237→        """Generate deterministic 2048D embedding from text.
   238→
   239→        Uses SHA-256 hash expanded to 2048D with sine wave modulation.
   240→
   241→        Args:
   242→            text: Input text to embed
   243→
   244→        Returns:
   245→            2048D numpy array with normalized values
   246→        """
   247→        # Generate hash
   248→        hash_obj = hashlib.sha256(text.encode())
   249→        hash_bytes = hash_obj.digest()
   250→
   251→        # Expand to 2048 dimensions using deterministic method
   252→        latent = np.zeros(self.HASH_DIMS)
   253→        for i in range(self.HASH_DIMS):
   254→            # Cycle through hash bytes
   255→            byte_idx = i % len(hash_bytes)
   256→            # Use sine wave modulation for smooth variation
   257→            phase = (2.0 * np.pi * i) / self.HASH_DIMS
   258→            latent[i] = (
   259→                (hash_bytes[byte_idx] / 255.0) * 0.5
   260→                + 0.25 * np.sin(phase)
   261→                + 0.25 * np.cos(phase * 2)
   262→            )
   263→
   264→        # Normalize to [-1, 1]
   265→        latent = 2.0 * (latent - np.min(latent)) / (np.max(latent) - np.min(latent) + 1e-8) - 1.0
   266→
   267→        return latent
   268→
   269→    def _holographic_project(self, latent_2048d: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
   270→        """Project 2048D embedding to 12D using holographic method.
   271→
   272→        Uses chunk-mean averaging: divide 2048D into 128-element segments
   273→        and take mean of each segment. Then interpolate to 12D.
   274→
   275→        Args:
   276→            latent_2048d: 2048D embedding vector
   277→
   278→        Returns:
   279→            12D normalized vector
   280→        """
   281→        # Check cache
   282→        latent_hash = hashlib.sha256(latent_2048d.tobytes()).hexdigest()[:8]
   283→        if latent_hash in self._projection_cache:
   284→            return self._projection_cache[latent_hash]
   285→
   286→        # Chunk-mean projection: 2048 → 16 dimensions (128-element chunks)
   287→        num_chunks = self.HASH_DIMS // self.CHUNK_SIZE
   288→        chunk_means = np.array(
   289→            [
   290→                np.mean(latent_2048d[i * self.CHUNK_SIZE : (i + 1) * self.CHUNK_SIZE])
   291→                for i in range(num_chunks)
   292→            ]
   293→        )
   294→
   295→        # Interpolate 16D → 12D
   296→        if len(chunk_means) > self.AXIOMATIC_DIMS:
   297→            # Downsample using linear interpolation
   298→            indices = np.linspace(0, len(chunk_means) - 1, self.AXIOMATIC_DIMS)
   299→            result_12d = np.interp(indices, np.arange(len(chunk_means)), chunk_means)
   300→        else:
   301→            # Upsample if needed
   302→            indices = np.linspace(0, len(chunk_means) - 1, self.AXIOMATIC_DIMS)
   303→            result_12d = np.interp(indices, np.arange(len(chunk_means)), chunk_means)
   304→
   305→        # Normalize to [0, 1]
   306→        result_12d = (result_12d - np.min(result_12d)) / (
   307→            np.max(result_12d) - np.min(result_12d) + 1e-8
   308→        )
   309→
   310→        # Cache result (evict oldest if at capacity)
   311→        if len(self._projection_cache) >= self.MAX_CACHE_SIZE:
   312→            oldest_key = next(iter(self._projection_cache))
   313→            del self._projection_cache[oldest_key]
   314→        self._projection_cache[latent_hash] = result_12d
   315→
   316→        return result_12d

   318→    def _step_to_axiomatic(
   319→        self,
   320→        projection_12d: np.ndarray,
   321→        operation_type: str,
   322→        coherence: float,
   323→        efficiency: float,
   324→    ) -> np.ndarray:
   325→        """Apply operation-specific modulation to 12D projection.
   326→
   327→        Combines base projection with operation modulation and
   328→        execution quality metrics.
   329→
   330→        Args:
   331→            projection_12d: 12D base projection
   332→            operation_type: Type of operation
   333→            coherence: Quality metric (0.0-1.0)
   334→            efficiency: Token efficiency (0.0-1.0)
   335→
   336→        Returns:
   337→            12D axiomatic vector
   338→        """
   339→        # Get modulation profile
   340→        operation_str = operation_type if isinstance(operation_type, str) else operation_type.value
   341→        modulation = self._modulation_profiles.get(
   342→            operation_str,
   343→            self._modulation_profiles[OperationType.TRANSFORM.value],
   344→        )
   345→
   346→        # Combine projection with modulation
   347→        # Weight modulation by execution quality
   348→        quality_weight = 0.5 * coherence + 0.5 * efficiency
   349→        axiomatic = projection_12d * (1.0 - quality_weight) + modulation * quality_weight
   350→
   351→        # Normalize
   352→        axiomatic = np.clip(axiomatic, 0.0, 1.0)
   353→
   354→        return axiomatic

   356→    def _compute_phi_score(
   357→        self,
   358→        coherence: float,
   359→        smoothness: float = 0.5,
   360→        convergence: float = 0.5,
   361→    ) -> float:
   362→        """Compute trajectory quality score (phi score).
   363→
   364→        Combines coherence (execution quality) with trajectory smoothness
   365→        and convergence (stability indicators).
   366→
   367→        Args:
   368→            coherence: Execution coherence metric
   369→            smoothness: Trajectory smoothness (0.0-1.0)
   370→            convergence: Convergence to stable state (0.0-1.0)
   371→
   372→        Returns:
   373→            Phi score (0.0-1.0)
   374→        """
   375→        phi = coherence * 0.5 + smoothness * 0.3 + convergence * 0.2
   376→        return np.clip(phi, 0.0, 1.0)

   378→    def track_execution(
   379→        self,
   380→        execution_result: ExecutionResult,
   381→        task_description: str,
   382→        operation_type: str,

   384→        """Track a compound execution as a trajectory point.
   385→
   386→        Args:
   387→            execution_result: ExecutionResult from compound executor
   388→            task_description: Description of the task
   389→            operation_type: Type of operation
   390→
   391→        Returns:
   392→            TrajectoryPoint with 12D trajectory coordinates
   393→        """
   394→        # Extract metrics
   395→        coherence = execution_result.metrics.get("coherence", 0.5)
   396→        efficiency = (
   397→            execution_result.token_metrics.get("cache_hit_rate", 0.5)
   398→            if execution_result.token_metrics
   399→            else 0.5
   400→        )
   401→
   402→        # Generate embeddings
   403→        latent_2048d = self._text_to_latent(task_description)
   404→        projection_12d = self._holographic_project(latent_2048d)
   405→
   406→        # Apply operation modulation
   407→        axiomatic_12d = self._step_to_axiomatic(
   408→            projection_12d, operation_type, coherence, efficiency
   409→        )
   410→
   411→        # Compute quality score using real trajectory history
   412→        smoothness = 0.5
   413→        convergence = 0.5
   414→        if len(self._recent_points) >= 2:
   415→            quality = self.compute_trajectory_quality(self._recent_points)
   416→            smoothness = quality["smoothness"]
   417→            convergence = quality["convergence"]
   418→
   419→        phi_score = self._compute_phi_score(
   420→            coherence=coherence,
   421→            smoothness=smoothness,
   422→            convergence=convergence,
   423→        )
   424→
   425→        point = TrajectoryPoint(
   426→            dimensions=axiomatic_12d,
   427→            timestamp=execution_result.duration_seconds,
   428→            coherence=coherence,
   429→            efficiency=efficiency,
   430→            operation_type=operation_type,
   431→            task_description=task_description,
   432→            metadata={

   434→                "success": execution_result.success,
   435→                "output_length": len(execution_result.output),
   436→            },
   437→        )
   438→
   439→        # Maintain recent points buffer (capped at window size)
   440→        self._recent_points.append(point)
   441→        if len(self._recent_points) > self.TRAJECTORY_WINDOW:
   442→            self._recent_points = self._recent_points[-self.TRAJECTORY_WINDOW :]
   443→
   444→        logger.debug(
   445→            "Tracked execution: %s (phi=%.2f, coherence=%.2f, "
   446→            "smoothness=%.2f, convergence=%.2f, buffer=%d)",
   447→            task_description[:50],
   448→            phi_score,
   449→            coherence,
   450→            smoothness,
   451→            convergence,
   452→            len(self._recent_points),
   453→        )
   454→
   455→        return point
